what does the Constitution say about a p.text:
According to the Nigerian Constitution, every person has a right to life, and no one shall be deprived intentionally of his life, save in execution of the sentence of a court in respect of a criminal offence of which he has been found guilty in Nigeria.

However, a person shall not be regarded as having been deprived of his life in contravention of this section, if he dies as a result of the use, to such extent and in such circumstances as are permitted by law, of such force as is reasonably necessary – (a) for the defence of any person from unlawful violence or for the defence of property: (b) in order to effect a lawful arrest or to prevent the escape of a person lawfully detained; or (c) for the purpose of suppressing a riot, insurrection or mutiny.

what penalty applies to a taxable person.text: A taxable person who fails or refuses to register for tax is liable to pay an administrative penalty of N50,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs, and N25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues.

citations.quote: APTER FOUR — OFFENCES AND PENALTIES PART I — OFFENCES AND PENALTIES OF GENERAL APPLICATION 100.—(1) A taxable person who fails or refuses to register for tax under section 4 of this Act, shall be liable to pay an administrative penalty of — (a) N50,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs ; and (b) N25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues.
